sources.entry: rs-short - Lightweight link shortener written in Rust, with features such as caching, spambot protection and phishing detection. (Demo) MPL-2.0 Rust

summary.name: rs-short
summary.one_liner: A minimal, lightweight self-hosted link shortener written in Rust on the Actix framework, with captcha, phishing detection and click counting.
use_cases: Running a private or organizational link shortener
Shortening links with spam and phishing protection
Hosting a lightweight URL shortener on a small server
Marking malicious short links with a warning page
Tracking click counts on shortened links without user tracking
summary.what_it_does: rs-short is a link shortener built in Rust with the Actix framework and server-side Askama templates. It uses no JavaScript or CSS framework, and the page says user IPs are not saved in the database. It stores data in SQLite by default, with PostgreSQL and MySQL available via build features. Features include a captcha against spam, active detection of suspicious (phishing) links, click counting, user deletion of their own shortcuts, and marking links as phishing to show a warning to victims. Admins can block URLs with regexes using a default blocklist, and caching is used to keep serving content during database locks.
notable: Around 1000 lines of Rust, uses 5-20MB of RAM, no JS and no unsafe code
Active phishing link detection and a warning page for links marked as phishing
Supports SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL; localized in French, English, Croatian and Occitan
Listed on awesome-selfhosted under URL Shorteners
caveats: SQLite default is marked as not for production use
Captcha is a basic spam protection and the page says more resilient spambot protection is a contribution area
Captcha cannot currently be disabled according to the contributing list
